title: "Benchmarks"

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

These timings come from `benchmarks/run.R`, run by the `benchmarks`
GitHub Actions workflow on one clean Ubuntu runner for the release and for
an earlier commit (`base`), one after the other. Times are medians of three
runs in seconds (one run for the slowest tasks); memory is what one run
allocates in R, in MiB, measured with `bench::bench_memory()`: not peak
memory, and native solver allocations are not included. The script also
records the status and objective of each result outside the timed runs. Solvers run with one
thread. Run the script yourself with `Rscript benchmarks/run.R`.

```{r}
dir <- "../../benchmarks/results"
new <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "new.csv"))
base <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "base.csv"))
# older result files name the memory column mb; it was MiB all along
for (nm in c("new", "base")) {
  d <- get(nm)
  if (is.null(d$mib)) d$mib <- d$mb
  assign(nm, d[c("group", "task", "size", "way", "seconds", "mib")])
}
tab <- merge(base, new, by = c("group", "task", "size", "way"),
             suffixes = c("_base", "_new"), sort = FALSE)
tab$speedup <- round(tab$seconds_base / pmax(tab$seconds_new, 1e-3), 1)
show <- function(g) {
  t <- tab[tab$group %in% g, c("task", "size", "way", "seconds_base",
                               "seconds_new", "speedup", "mib_base", "mib_new")]
  knitr::kable(t, row.names = FALSE,
               col.names = c("task", "size", "way", "s (base)", "s",
                             "speedup", "MiB (base)", "MiB"))
}
```

```{r, results = "asis"}
cat(readLines(file.path(dir, "platform.txt")), sep = "\n")
```

## Building models

Construction paths are linear in the size of the model: concatenation,
indicator constraints, quadratic rows (stored as one triplet table) and
variables added one at a time no longer copy what is already there, and a
sparse coefficient matrix stays sparse in `A %*% x`.

```{r}
show("construction")
```

## Linear and mixed-integer programs

The same model solved through optcompR, through the solver's own R package
and through ROI. The difference to the direct call is the cost of building,
classifying and checking the model.

```{r}
show(c("LP", "MILP"))
```

## Quadratic and nonlinear programs

Automatic selection sends convex QPs to Clarabel: the HiGHS active set QP
solver needs thousands of iterations at a few thousand variables.

```{r}
show(c("QP", "NLP"))
```

## Repeated solves and derivatives

After `opt_set_parameter()`, lowered blocks whose parameters did not change
are reused, and the HiGHS solver and OSQP workspace of the previous solve are
updated in place. For the QP below, setting up a new OSQP workspace is cheap
next to the rest of each solve, so keeping it gains nothing measurable.

```{r}
show(c("repeated", "derivatives"))
```
